Grenada 770 (Telescope Estate)

Claim Details, Associated Individuals and Estates

24th Oct 1836 | 206 Enslaved | £6212 0s 3d

Claim Details

Claim Notes

Parliamentary Papers p. 312.

T71/880: claim by Richard Purcell, in right of his wife, owner-in-fee. Counterclaim by Thomson Hankey, John Alexander Hankey and Thomson Hankey junior, of Mincing Lane, merchants, as mortgagees by an assignment of 08/09/1826 and as creditors by several judgements dated 06/04/1830. Counterclaim from Michael Lindsay and William Lindsay, of Cloghans [?], near Tuam Galway, Ireland, as legatees under the will of Thomas Lindsay senior and Thomas Lindsay junior.

Large volume of correspondence from Michael Lindsay, 'stating that he is Executor of will of Thos. Lindsay junior and submitting that he is the proper party to "settle with"'; 'Letter from Michael Lindsay of Cloghans...requesting information and stating that his co-counterclaimants Willm & Patrick Lindsay have no interest in the above claim and that by refusing to withdraw their claim, they prevent him making arrangements with claimant'; 'Report of Assistant Commissioners that two slaves Frank & Francois had been illegally registered and held in slavery' .

T71/1593 p. 95: letter, dated 05/02/1836, to M. Lindsay, Cloghans, Hollymount, County Mayo, suggesting he appoint an agent.

T71/1593 p. 297: letter, dated 17/10/1836, to W. Ross Lewin, 14 Shaftesbury Terrace, Pimlico, referring to this claim, and warning him that the Hankeys were intending to issue process on W. Ross Lewin to attend.

T71/1592 p. 195: letter, dated 07/03/1835, from which it appears that W. Ross Lewin, of 17 Upper Berkeley St. West, was acting on behalf of Messrs, 'Lydsy' (Lyndsay).

T71/1592 p. 211: letter, dated 22/08/1835, from the Court of Chancery to Messrs. P. and W. Lindsay, responding to the Lindsays' petition (and offering to put it into a counterclaim form?).

Documents of Interest

Windsor and Williamsfield Inventory of Slaves 1814 p8

Document comprises 4 parts, written recto and verso across 5 folios: 1. An inventory and valuation of enslaved persons at Windsor Estate, St Elizabeth parish, Jamaica, 1814. 2. An inventory and valuation of enslaved persons at Williamsfield settlement, St Elisabeth parish, Jamaica, 1814. 3. An inventory of animals at Windsor Estate, St Elizabeth parish, Jamaica, 1814. 4. A cover note outlining the contents of the document.
